source: A watermark is a statistical signal embedded during sampling. Detection compares the observed token choices with the choices the key would have favoured, so the test needs enough tokens to separate the signal from chance.
candidate: Watermarking embeds a statistical signal while the model samples. To detect it, you compare the tokens that appeared with those the key would have preferred, which means short passages carry too little evidence to separate the mark from noise.

source: Renewable energy projects often face long permitting timelines. A solar farm may need environmental review, grid connection studies, and local approval before construction begins, and each stage can take months. Developers argue that predictable rules would lower financing costs, while residents ask for time to review visual and land-use effects.
candidate: Permitting for renewable projects tends to be slow. Before building a solar farm, a developer may need an environmental review, a grid connection study, and local approval, and any of these can take months.
